question.text: In the same Pay-for-Success through Grants structure, if the NPO does NOT achieve the pre-defined outcomes AND the pre-defined time period is over, the CSR capital in the escrow is:

answer.text: Refunded to the CSR funder without any onward deployment.
Paid to the interim funding partner as compensation for non-performance.
Routed to items provided under Schedule VII of the Companies Act such as the PM's Relief Fund.
Transferred to the SSE Investor Protection Fund.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 2.3.1.1(c), if the NPO has not achieved outcomes and the pre-defined time period is over, the CSR funder 'routes the CSR capital to items provided under Schedule VII of the Companies Act such as the PM's Relief Fund'. If the time period is NOT yet over, it rolls over in escrow. This preserves the CSR deployment requirement under Section 135. **The Trap:** Option A would violate Section 135 CSR compliance. Option B rewards non-performance — the interim funder bears its own risk. Option D invents a fund that does not exist for CSR under-performance. **Cross-Exam Context:** V-A (MF Distributor), X-A/X-B (IA) treat CSR routing compliance. III-A/III-C (Compliance) track Schedule VII activity lists. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When your outcome-failure report lands, annotate the recommended redeployment target (PM's Relief Fund or other Schedule VII items) in the SIR — CSR funders often seek this from the SIA because your independent sign-off supports their Section 135 disclosure on 'reasons for shortfall'.
